summary: Tao Jiang works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo and was an associate professor of religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
Tao Jin is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He earned his PhD in 2008 at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan specializes in Indology and linguistics. He completed a BA at Fudan University in 2010 and earned a Magister Artium at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.
Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. From circa 1971 to 1998, he served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library and held a post at the University of Copenhagen.

Tarif Khalidi (born 1938) is a historian and scholar of religion. He studied at University College, Oxford (~1957–1960) and the University of Chicago (~1960–1963), later holding posts at the American University of Beirut (~1970–1996) and the University of Cambridge (~1996–2002).

Tarthang Tulku (born 1935) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers including A-'gyur Rinpoche, founded the Nyingma Institute, and served as Head Lama at Padma Ling (~1969), the Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center (~1969), and the Nyingma Institute (~1972).

Tashi Tsering (born 1960) works in Tibetology, linguistics, and history. He studied under Burmiok Athing and Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche, founded the Amnye Machen Institute, and held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Tatiana Oranskaia (born 1950) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and held a professorship at the University of Hamburg from circa 2004 to 2015.

Tatsugen Sato (1924–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology. He held academic posts at Komazawa University as an assistant professor (attested 1972–1978) and professor (attested 1994), alongside teaching roles at Ryukoku University and Tokai University.
Tatsuhiro Saito specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.
Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012) was a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1948 to 1953 and later served as a professor there (attested 1996).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat (born 1950) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaii, studied under Luang Por Teean Jittasubho, and held positions at Kyoto University, Mahidol University, and the World Buddhist University.

Tej Ram Sharma (born 1941) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (attested 1978).

Tensei Kitabatake (1928–2024) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1948–1953). He later served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1974–1997) and held posts at Otani, Kyoto Women's, Tenri, and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen universities.
Tenshin Tanouye (1938–2003) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under traditional teacher Sogen Omori and founded Chozen-ji.
Tenzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Tenzin earned a Master of Philosophy at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa. He served as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and at Pullahari Monastery.

Tenzin Gyatso, 14th Dalai Lama (born 1935), specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sera and Drepung monasteries, Melbourne, British Columbia, and under teachers including Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Dilgo Khyentse, Trijang, and Trulshik.

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche (born 1961) works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a Geshe degree at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (~1979–1986), where he served as president, and later was a Rockefeller Fellow at Rice University (1991).

Ter Ellingson (born 1944) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Concordia College (1966), the University of Chicago (1970), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1979), and served on the faculty at the University of Washington (1981–2016).
